Ill. Predicate Devices
The HT7O is substantially equivalent to the following legally marketed predicate
devices:
* NEWPORT HT70® Ventilator cleared under K090888;
* CareFusion LTV0 1200 cleared under K060647;
* Versamed Medical Systems iVENTTM 201 cleared under K073694.
IV. Device Description
The Newport HT70 Ventilator provides ventilatory support for neonate, infant,
pediatric and adult patients. It can be used in hospital, sub-acute, emergency
response, transport and homecare environments under the direction of a
physician. The HT70 ventilator design provides maximum mobility and safety for
short or long distance transport of critically ill patients and also for patients who
are going about their normal activities of daily life.
The HT7O may be operated from AC or DC external power sources or from the
integrated battery system. Any time the ventilator is connected to external
power, the integrated battery system is charged, including while the ventilator is
in use. The HT7O ventilator has AJCMV, SIMV and SPONT ventilatory modes
(Pressure or Volume).
The controls of the HT70 ventilator are easily found on the front touch screen and
panel. The touch screen can be set up in Hospital, Transport or Basic functional
Domains to provide the user with full or limited access. The HT70 has a Trends
screen for displaying data graphically. User Help screens present information for
all controls and features.
V. Intended Use
The Newport HT7O family of ventilators is intended to provide continuous or
intermittent positive pressure mechanical ventilatory support for the care of
individuals who require mechanical ventilation through invasive or non-invasive
interfaces. Specifically, the Newport HT70 family of ventilators is applicable for
infant, pediatric and adult patients greater than or equal to 5 kg (11 Ibs).
The Newport HT70 is a restricted medical device intended for use by qualified,
trained personnel under the direction of a physician.
The Newport HT70 is suitable for use in hospital, sub-acute, emergency room,
and home care environments, as well as for transport and emergency response
applications.
VI. Reason for the Submission
The purpose of this traditional 510(k) is to request authorization for enhancement
to the Newport HT70 ventilator to include the following features:
" On-airway flow sensor for exhaled volume monitoring and flow trigger
* SP02 monitoring using a cleared accessory device.
The Newport HT70 ventilator has been determined to be substantially equivalent
to other legally marketed predicate ventilators. The HT7O ventilator is an
extension of the current HT70 design and technology.
VII. Nonclinical Data
The Newport HT70 ventilator has undergone extensive verification, validation
and design safety testing, all of which confirms that the device meets its design,
performance, and safety requirements.
VilI. Conclusions
All testing demonstrates that the Newport HT7O performs as intended and has
acceptable mechanical properties when used in accordance with its labeling; the
device is therefore suitable for its intended use. As the device's intended use is
comparable to the referenced predicate devices, and its operating principles,
ventilation modes and performance parameters are comparable to the predicate
devices, the HT7O is substantially equivalent to the predicate devices.
